Hi Sean,

Thanks for taking this — we’re kicking off our vendor risk review for the new inference provider evaluation. Two asks to start:

1) Can you share Redwood’s latest SOC 2 Type II report (covering at least the last 12-month period) and confirm the audit period covered?

2) We need explicit confirmation of how SOC 2 coverage maps to Redwood hosting modes: Hosted (multi-tenant API), Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU pools), and Private/VPC or on-prem installs. Specifically: which modes are fully in-scope of your SOC 2 report, which require a bridge letter or addendum, and any limitations (e.g., routing/fallback paths that could touch multi-tenant hosts).

We have a compliance deadline of 31 Aug to complete initial evidence collection. If you can get this to us this week that would be ideal. If a short call is easier, happy to schedule.

Sean / Rachel — fyi and draft responses below that I recommend we send to Commercia. I’ve attached a draft bridge letter and the 2026 SOC 2 Type II PDF to the internal doc store (see links).

TL;DR (for the outbound):
- SOC 2 Type II report scope: covers Redwood’s control plane and production runtime for Hosted API and Dedicated reserved GPU pools we operate as part of Redwood-managed infrastructure. Audit period: 2026-01-01 to 2026-12-31 (Type II).
- Private / VPC / on-prem: typically out-of-scope for the Redwood SOC 2 report when the customer manages the compute and network (customer-managed VPCs / air-gapped installs). We can support with: (a) a bridge letter that documents mapping of controls for Dedicated pools where isolation and tenant mapping exists; or (b) tailored evidence packages and an SOC bridge demonstrating where responsibility splits exist.
- Edge cases: if a Private deployment uses Redwood's managed control plane (e.g., for updates or routing), that control plane component *is* in-scope; we will call these out explicitly in the mapping doc.

Attachments included for outbound: Draft_Bridge_Letter_Commercia.docx (please redline), Redwood_SOC2_TypeII_2026.pdf, hosting-network-diagram.png.

Next steps I propose:
1) Sean to send a short outbound email to Alice with attachments and invite to a 30-min call (AuditOps optional).
2) If Commercia needs an attestation specific to their Dedicated pool mapping, we prepare a 1–2 page addendum (2–3 business days).

Laura — tagging you for any legal phrasing we should avoid in the bridge letter (e.g., absolute “coverage” language).

Alice — attaching the items Marcus referenced. See attachments and short notes below. Happy to walk through on a quick call if helpful.

Attachments (attached):
- Redwood_SOC2_TypeII_2026.pdf — SOC 2 Type II report (audit period 2026-01-01 to 2026-12-31). Redactions applied for sensitive third-party details.
- Draft_Bridge_Letter_Commercia.docx — bridge letter template that explains applicability of controls to Dedicated/Reserved pools and the boundaries for Private/VPC installs. Please redline where language needs to be tighter.
- hosting-network-diagram.png — simplified diagram we typically share with auditors showing tenancy boundaries for Dedicated pools.

Notes / quick clarifications:
- Hosted (multi-tenant API): fully in-scope of the report.
- Redwood Dedicated (Redwood-managed reserved pools): in-scope when the compute and network are operated by Redwood and tenant mapping is enforced; the bridge letter documents the mapping for reserved pools that host a single tenant or a pinned set of tenants.
- Private / VPC / On-prem: out-of-scope for the standard SOC 2 report when customers manage the compute/network. If Redwood manages the control plane (e.g., centralized key management, update service), those specific control plane functions remain in-scope — we call these out explicitly in the mapping doc.

Proposed next steps:
1) Please review the draft bridge letter and redline by Wed 25 Aug.
2) If you need an attestation specific to your Dedicated pool mapping, we can prepare a 1–2 page addendum within 2 business days of receipt of your details (pool IDs, tenant mapping).
3) If helpful, I’ll schedule a 30-min call with our AuditOps lead (copied) to walk through the artifacts.
